data.content_ref: inline:SRC_003's mechanism claims a large service can 'always replicate independent components (strictly more redundancy),' treating redundancy as a strict superset of the decentralized capacity. But the target's own countercondition concedes the large service may be unable to achieve the same diversity due to internal standardization pressures. Under that condition, the large service cannot replicate the small services' causal heterogeneity even though it has more total components. The conclusion that the large service's redundancy is 'strictly superior' therefore lacks a causal mechanism: it assumes component replication implies diversity replication, which the admitted countercondition refutes. The barrier-versus-redundancy framing does not supply the missing causal link between 'more components' and 'more resilience to correlated failure' when standardization causes a common-mode dependency the small services avoid.
